key_insight: A 9-qubit superconducting processor with Platonic lattice connectivity was used to digitally simulate 3D Ising criticality and recover critical exponents close to theory.
engineering_relevance: This work shows that nontrivial qubit connectivity plus phase-sensitive variational methods can make small quantum hardware useful for studying hard many-body physics with high spectral precision.
method: Encoded the cubic transverse-field Ising model on an 8-qubit register within a multiply connected Platonic lattice.
Used an extended VQE with a phase-based loss function to variationally prepare low-energy eigenstates.
Extracted the four lowest eigenenergies via Fourier analysis and numerical fitting.
evidence_signal: The extracted eigenenergies matched exact diagonalization within about ±0.001, yielding Delta_epsilon = 1.5850 and nu = 0.7067.
watch_item: The approach currently relies on a small, specialized qubit topology and careful spectral fitting, so scaling to larger lattices may be challenging.
paper_title: 3D Ising criticality with Platonic lattice superconducting qubits
